source: Chapter VI screenplay + canonical storyboard; F01 and F02 separate single-image author turns

scenes.focus: one miniature enclosed railway freight wagon is positioned by a dark-gloved investigator's hand on a weathered railway route drawing with three distinct marked locations, visually comparing known observations with an unresolved branch
scenes.camera: tight angled overhead shot of the paper rail plan on a detective's wooden table, with the one wagon token and three marked locations in sharp focus, face of the investigator completely unseen
scenes.location: a rain-shadowed private detective's office in industrial Birmingham in the 1920s
required: exactly one small dark brass freight-wagon model held between gloved fingers on the paper route
a single hand-drawn rail map with three distinct circular stop marks connected by one branching railway line, two checked points and one uncertain mark
a metal engineer's ruler and a plain mechanical drafting pen near the bottom of the map
scenes.background: old wooden worktable, worn railway ledgers, cast-metal desk lamp and rain-streaked window with distant smoke-blackened brick mills
scenes.light: focused warm amber desk-lamp illumination across aged paper and dark gloves against cool blue rainy industrial dusk
scenes.npc: one anonymous investigator visible only by dark wool sleeves and black leather gloves, no face and no other people
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The map distinguishes recorded observations from assumptions. Only one wagon and one rail journey exist. The image never proves disappearance, witness movements, a final wagon location, or completion of the investigation.
avoid: multiple wagons, a train arriving at a documented destination, or witnesses physically appearing on the map
a stamped official declaration that the wagon disappeared or reached a secret station
recognizable face or altered canonical appearance of any selectable hero
readable invented station names, routes, times, or new witness addresses

scenes.focus: an anonymous gloved investigator compares two separate old freight documents, one with flowing cursive and a light seal, the other with a tightly ruled arrival ledger and a different official seal, without joining the pages together
scenes.camera: an oblique close overhead view across a dark desk, both weathered sheets held separately in each gloved hand with the center gap clearly visible, face of the investigator fully out of frame
scenes.location: the rain-facing worktable of a modest railway investigator in industrial Birmingham during the 1920s
required: one aged left-hand freight paper dominated by flowing cursive pen strokes and a low round stamp
one separate right-hand train arrival ledger sheet dominated by tight ruled columns, a different script and its own stamp impression
two black-gloved hands keeping both paper sheets physically separate above a scratched oak table
scenes.background: a heavy brass oil desk lamp, old ink bottle, magnifying glass, closed railway ledger and a rain-wet window overlooking smoke-belching brick factories
scenes.light: an intense warm amber desk lamp across the two independent papers, contrasting with the cold blue industrial rain beyond the window
scenes.npc: only the investigator's black leather gloves and dark sleeves appear; no identifiable face or other human figures
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: These are two independent suspected falsifications, not one merged forged document. The image does not prove either account false, confirm a second forgery, establish which witness signed, reveal the whereabouts of the wagon, or identify a culprit.
avoid: readable invented signatures, witness names, fabricated station names, amounts or dates
one single joint forged sheet replacing the two materially distinct documents
an official verdict, celebratory conclusion, verified guilty party or definitive forensic proof
recognizable face or altered canonical appearance of any selectable investigator
